rationale: X's findings (mel_head bias, s2mel zero-audio fallback, full-payload concat semantics, snapshot_mm_payload) are detailed but almost entirely orthogonal to the ground-truth reviewers' actual concerns (benchmark-script duplication, missing profiler/VRAM evidence, native-speed streaming validation asymmetry, duration_factor bound duplication/consistency). Y engages more directly with GT-adjacent territory (validates native-speed streaming behavior, flags stale docs/serving/speech_api.md contradicting the new HTTP speed exception — echoing GT's WebSocket/HTTP asymmetry comment) and grounds nearly every finding with literal quoted file:line evidence, making it more verifiable and precise. Both are reasonably actionable with concrete file:line targets, but Y's evidence-first format and closer thematic overlap with the human reviewers' concerns give it the edge on recall and precision.
